To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

site-specific radiation damage can be modelled and refined, that the phasing power is limited by the overall radiation damage, and that the phasing process can be improved by reducing the time required for recording the complete data set.

site-specific radiation damage can be used to improve the phases in MAD and SAD experiments, but that the quality of the final phases will ultimately be determined by the overall radiation damage that occurs during the experiment.
site-specific radiation damage can be used to phase a structure, and that this approach is most successful in cases where the effects of overall damage can be minimized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new phasing approach that allows to make full use of site-specific radiation-damage effects in SAD or MAD experiments.
the development of a method for the phasing of macromolecular structures from SAD/MAD data that is applicable in the presence of site-specific radiation effects.
the development of methods for the modelling of site-specific radiation-damage effects in MAD/SAD phasing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the site-specific radiation damage approach can be used in a wide range of cases, but that it is not necessarily a panacea in all situations.

site-specific radiation damage can only be used as an additional source of phasing information when the total time required to record a MAD data set is shorter than the time scale on which overall radiation damage unfolds.
site-specific radiation damage is a powerful and useful tool to enhance the phasing of difficult structures, provided that the effects of overall damage are kept at a tolerable level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phasing power that is obtained from site-specific radiation damage is limited by the effects that are caused by overall radiation damage.

, in the case of site-specific radiation-damage phasing, the quality of the resulting phases is not only determined by the amount of site-specific radiation-induced disorder but also by the amount of overall radiation-induced disorder.

site-specific radiation damage can provide additional phasing power, but that this power can only be exploited in a meaningful manner if overall radiation damage is minimized and/or if site-specific radiation damage is monitored in a quantitative manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phasing power of site-specific radiation damages can be fully exploited by the use of appropriate models for the description and refinement of the radiation damage process.
, for site-specific radiation damage, the phasing information is generated through the evolution of the site-specific intensity differences as a function of irradiation time.
site-specific radiation damage can be used to obtain additional phase information in SAD/Mad experiments, provided that the effects of overall damage are kept under control.
